editorial:
You meet three longtime friends who seem to have everything figured out. Max, Paul, and Simon have shared vacations, card nights, and drinks for 35 years, so their bond feels easy and lived-in. That comfort makes Simon's sudden confession hit hard: he says he strangled his wife, Estelle, after a huge fight. The movie turns a normal guys' night into a tense moral puzzle, mixing dark humor with real panic. You watch two ordinary men try to decide if loyalty to a friend can ever excuse covering up something terrible.

The acting carries the film, with the three leads making every argument feel personal and messy. The pacing stays tight, and the humor comes from awkward reactions rather than big jokes. It is not a fast action movie, so viewers wanting thrills may find it slow. Still, if you like character-driven stories and ethical dilemmas, it is worth your time. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, Simon's request for an alibi forces Max and Paul to stop avoiding the truth. Their friendship cracks as they weigh protecting Simon against doing the right thing. The ending focuses on the fallout of that choice rather than a neat rescue, showing how one violent night changes all three men and leaves their old routine behind.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves small-cast dramas about friendship, guilt, and hard choices.
